grades.quote: Multiple page table entries can point to the same page frame. In the extreme case, an entire virtual address space of 2<sup>64</sup> bytes could be made readable as zeros by having all the page table entries marked read-only and pointed at a single zeroed-out page frame.
grades.reason: Directly demonstrates that a huge virtual range can use little physical memory through shared backing, but does not explain sparse unmapped regions.
Describes application address limits, not why sparse virtual ranges require little physical memory.

grades.quote: The table need not contain a physical address translation for every page of virtual addresses; in effect, some entries can be left blank.
grades.reason: Explains that not every virtual page needs physical backing; the passage also describes installing translations only when needed.

grades.quote: This limited sharing may be a way for the processes to communicate, or it may simply be a way to reduce memory consumption and the time needed to initialize memory. Regardless of the motivation, the shared physical memory can occupy a different range of virtual addresses in each process.
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary context about shared physical backing, but does not explain how sparsity separates address-range size from physical-memory use.
